primary.title: The Edict of Milan
primary.author: Constantine the Great and Licinius
primary.rationale: This is a foundational document for religious tolerance in the Roman Empire, issued by Constantine and Licinius. While not a direct speech or letter solely by Constantine, it is directly attributed to his reign and policy.

primary.title: Letter of Constantine to the Church of Nicomedia
primary.author: Constantine the Great
primary.rationale: This letter, preserved by Eusebius, discusses the construction of churches and Constantine's religious views, offering insight into his policies and personal beliefs.

primary.title: Address to the Saints
primary.author: Constantine the Great
primary.rationale: A speech attributed to Constantine, delivered at the Council of Nicaea, though its authenticity and exact wording are debated by scholars. It reflects his engagement with Christian doctrine.

secondary.title: Constantine the Great: Emperor, Christian, Revolutionary
secondary.author: Paul Stephenson
secondary.rationale: A comprehensive and well-regarded scholarly biography of Constantine, published by a major academic press, offering modern analysis of his reign and impact.

secondary.title: The Cambridge Companion to the Age of Constantine
secondary.author: Noel Lenski
secondary.rationale: An edited volume featuring essays by leading scholars on various aspects of Constantine's era, providing diverse scholarly perspectives on his rule and its consequences.

secondary.title: Constantine's Conversion: Historical, Literary, and Theological Reinterpretations
secondary.author: Paul J. Fedwick
secondary.rationale: This collection of essays critically examines the complex and debated topic of Constantine's conversion, offering scholarly analysis from multiple viewpoints.

suggestions.notes: Primary sources attributed to Constantine are often preserved through the writings of others, such as Eusebius of Caesarea. Direct, independently preserved texts are rare. Availability on digital archives like Internet Archive is more likely than on Project Gutenberg or Wikisource for these specific historical documents.
